This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: ANSWER ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: ANSWER ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0, Mg = 24.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 $\mathrm{cm^3}$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 $\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}C^{-1}}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 273\ \mathrm{K}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sketch and name the laboratory apparatus used during acid/base titration to

(i) Transfer $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of a base into a conical flask

(ii) Prepare a standard solution. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Pipette** (a $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ bulb or volumetric pipette, used with a pipette filler). *Sketch:* a long thin glass tube with a wide bulb in the middle, a single engraved ring mark on the upper neck and a narrow jet at the bottom. *Use:* rinse it with the base, draw the base up above the mark, adjust the bottom of the meniscus to the mark, then let it drain into the conical flask with the tip touching the inside wall (do not blow out the last drop).

(ii) **Volumetric (graduated) flask.** *Sketch:* a flat-bottomed, pear-shaped flask with a long narrow neck carrying a single ring mark (e.g. $250\ \mathrm{cm^3}$) and a stopper. *Use:* weigh the solute exactly on a balance; dissolve it in a little distilled water in a beaker with a glass rod; pour the solution through a funnel into the volumetric flask; rinse the beaker, rod and funnel into the flask; add distilled water (with a wash bottle or dropper) until the bottom of the meniscus is on the mark; stopper and invert several times to mix.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In a titration experiment, a student transferred $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of sodium carbonate solution into a conical flask and titrated with dilute hydrochloric acid run from an equipment, P.

(i) Draw and name equipment P. *[2 marks]*

(ii) The following table shows results of two accurate titrations.

| | Titration 1 | Titration 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Second reading of P | 24.8 | 44.6 |
| First reading of P | 2.5 | 22.4 |
| Titre volume | | |

Complete the table and determine the volume of dilute hydrochloric acid used. *[2 marks]*

Calculate the concentration of sodium carbonate solution if 0.1M HCl was used for the titration. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Methyl orange is used for this titration. What colour change is observed at the end point? Initial colour: ... Final colour: ... *[2 marks]*

(iv) During an acid-base titration, how many times do we usually carry out the titration process? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Burette.** *Sketch:* a long, narrow, graduated glass tube (0 to $50\ \mathrm{cm^3}$) held vertically in a clamp on a retort stand, with a tap (stopcock) at the bottom and a small funnel at the top; the conical flask stands on a white tile under the jet.

(ii) Titre volume = second reading $-$ first reading:

| | Titration 1 | Titration 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Second reading of P | 24.8 | 44.6 |
| First reading of P | 2.5 | 22.4 |
| Titre volume | **22.3** | **22.2** |

Both titres agree within $0.1\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, so the volume of acid used is the mean: $\dfrac{22.3 + 22.2}{2} =$ **22.25 $\mathrm{cm^3}$**.

*Concentration of sodium carbonate.* Equation: $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow 2NaCl + H_2O + CO_2}$ (balanced: Na 2, C 1, O 3, H 2, Cl 2 each side of the 1 : 2 ratio).

Moles of HCl $= 0.1 \times \dfrac{22.25}{1000} = 2.225\times10^{-3}$ mol.

Mole ratio $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3} : \mathrm{HCl} = 1 : 2$, so moles of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ $= \dfrac{2.225\times10^{-3}}{2} = 1.1125\times10^{-3}$ mol in $25\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

Concentration $= \dfrac{1.1125\times10^{-3}}{25} \times 1000 =$ **0.0445 mol dm$^{-3}$** (about 0.045 M).

(iii) **Initial colour: yellow** (the sodium carbonate solution is alkaline). **Final colour: orange** (the first permanent orange / pinkish-orange tint at the end point; excess acid turns it red).

(iv) Usually **three times**: one rough (trial) titration to find the approximate end point, then two or more accurate titrations until two titres agree within $0.1\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ (concordant results); the mean of the concordant titres is used.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an experiment to determine the formula of an oxide of copper, the following results were obtained.

Mass of boat alone = 8.320 g

Mass of boat and oxide = 10.87 g

Mass of boat and copper = 10.368 g

Determine the formula of the oxide of copper. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Relative atomic masses: Cu = 64.0, O = 16.0.

Mass of oxide $= 10.87 - 8.320 = 2.550$ g. Mass of copper $= 10.368 - 8.320 = 2.048$ g. Mass of oxygen $= 2.550 - 2.048 = 0.502$ g.

| | Cu | O |
|---|---|---|
| Mass (g) | 2.048 | 0.502 |
| Moles | $\dfrac{2.048}{64.0} = 0.0320$ | $\dfrac{0.502}{16.0} = 0.0314$ |
| Ratio (divide by 0.0314) | 1.02 | 1 |

The ratio is $1 : 1$ to the nearest whole number, so the empirical formula is **CuO** (copper(II) oxide).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A gas X is as soluble in water as ammonia.

Draw the apparatus that a student will use to dissolve gas X in water. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A very soluble gas is dissolved with an **inverted funnel** to avoid suck-back of water into the gas supply.

*Sketch:* the gas delivery tube leads to a thistle (filter) funnel turned upside down, with its wide rim just touching the surface of the water in a beaker (the rim only just dips below the surface). Label: gas X in, inverted funnel, beaker, water.

The funnel gives a large surface for the gas to dissolve; if the gas dissolves quickly and the water rises, the level in the funnel falls below the rim, air breaks the seal, and the water cannot be sucked back into the generating flask.
